config.title: PropTypes / TypeScript Interface

intro.title: PropTypes / TypeScript Interface
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple user profile card component that displays a person's name, age, and email. You will learn how to define and use TypeScript interfaces to specify the expected data types for the component's props. This ensures your component receives the correct data structure and helps catch errors early during development. The main technologies involved are React with TypeScript, focusing on type safety and component prop validation.
intro.usecase: In real-world applications like e-commerce dashboards or data-heavy admin panels, components such as product cards, data tables, and filter controls must reliably receive and display specific data types. Using PropTypes or TypeScript interfaces ensures that components like a user profile modal or a settings form receive the correct props—like a user object with a required `id` (number) and `name` (string)—preventing runtime errors. This pattern is crucial for maintaining code quality in team projects, where clear contracts between components help avoid bugs when integrating features like search filters or dynamic charts, leading to more robust and maintainable software.

objectives: Apply TypeScript interfaces to define the expected shape of component props.
Implement PropTypes to specify and validate the types of props passed to a component.
Configure a React component to accept props defined by a TypeScript interface.
Update a component to use PropTypes for runtime type checking in a development environment.
Construct a component that integrates both TypeScript static typing and PropTypes validation.
Manipulate props by applying default values using PropTypes or optional interface properties.
Render a component with props that are validated through both TypeScript and PropTypes.

steps.title: Import React and create a basic component
steps.instruction: Import React from 'react' and create a functional component named UserProfile that returns an empty div.
steps.hint: Start by writing the import statement, then define your component. You can use either a function declaration or an arrow function.
steps.seedCode: // Import React and create the UserProfile component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A functional component named UserProfile is created and ready to be enhanced with props and types in later steps.
successCriteria: React is imported from 'react', and a component named UserProfile returns an empty div.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've imported React and created a component named UserProfile that returns an empty div element.
steps.feedbackWrong: import React from 'react' and create a functional component called UserProfile that returns an empty div.

steps.title: Define props using TypeScript interface
steps.instruction: Create a TypeScript interface called UserProfileProps with three properties: name (string), age (number), and isActive (boolean).
steps.hint: Define the interface above your component. Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and property definitions.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a TypeScript interface that defines the shape of props your component will accept.
successCriteria: A UserProfileProps interface is defined with name (string), age (number), and isActive (boolean) properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that all three properties (name, age, isActive) are included with the correct TypeScript types.
steps.feedbackWrong: The interface isn't defined correctly. Make sure to use the 'interface' keyword and include all three properties with their types.

steps.title: Apply the interface to component props
steps.instruction: Add the UserProfileProps interface as the type for the UserProfile component's props parameter.
steps.hint: In TypeScript, you can type the props parameter by adding a colon and the interface name after the parameter.
steps.expectedOutcome: The UserProfile component should now have typed props using the UserProfileProps interface.
successCriteria: The UserProfile component's props parameter is typed with the UserProfileProps interface.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to add the type annotation to the props parameter. Try adding ': UserProfileProps' after the props parameter.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component's props aren't typed yet. Remember to add the interface name after the props parameter with a colon.

steps.title: Display props in the component markup
steps.instruction: Update the UserProfile component to display the name, age, and isActive props from the UserProfileProps interface in the returned JSX.
steps.hint: Access the props by destructuring them in the component function parameters, then use curly braces {} to embed their values in the JSX.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will display the user's name, age, and active status in the UI when props are passed.
successCriteria: The component destructures name, age, and isActive from props and displays each value in the JSX using curly braces.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're displaying all three props (name, age, isActive) in the JSX.
steps.feedbackWrong: The props aren't being displayed correctly. Check that you're destructuring them in the function parameters and using curly braces to embed their values.

steps.title: Create ProductCard and its props interface
steps.instruction: Create a TypeScript interface named ProductCardProps with required props title (string) and price (number). Also create a functional component named ProductCard that uses this interface.
steps.hint: Define ProductCardProps above ProductCard. Type the component props as ProductCardProps and render title and price in JSX.
steps.expectedOutcome: A typed ProductCardProps interface and ProductCard component are defined and ready for extension.
successCriteria: ProductCardProps interface is defined with title and price. ProductCard is a functional component typed with ProductCardProps.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure ProductCardProps has title and price, and ProductCard uses that interface in its props.
steps.feedbackWrong: Define ProductCardProps first (title: string, price: number), then create ProductCard using ProductCardProps.

steps.title: Use optional props with TypeScript
steps.instruction: In the existing ProductCardProps interface, add an optional 'description' prop (type string). Display it conditionally in ProductCard markup.
steps.hint:
Edit the already-declared ProductCardProps interface (do not create a new interface). Use description?: string and render with description &&

{description}

.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ProductCard component interface includes an optional 'description' prop, and the component conditionally renders it when provided.
successCriteria: ProductCardProps interface has an optional 'description?: string' prop. The ProductCard component uses conditional rendering to display the description only when it exists.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the description prop is marked as optional with '?' in the interface and you're using conditional rendering to display it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The optional prop wasn't properly added. Review how to mark props as optional in TypeScript interfaces and how to conditionally render content.

steps.title: Add PropTypes as an alternative approach
steps.instruction: Import PropTypes from 'prop-types' at the top of your file.
steps.hint: Add the import statement above your existing code. This will allow you to use PropTypes for runtime type checking alongside TypeScript.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing a library for validation
import PropTypes from 'prop-types';
steps.expectedOutcome: The PropTypes library is imported, making it available for runtime type validation in your components.
successCriteria: PropTypes is imported from 'prop-types' at the top of the file.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're importing from 'prop-types' (with a hyphen) and using the correct import syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement for PropTypes is missing or incorrect. Remember to import PropTypes from 'prop-types'.

steps.title: Compare TypeScript vs PropTypes
steps.instruction: Add PropTypes to the UserProfile component while keeping the TypeScript interface.
steps.hint: Import PropTypes from 'prop-types' and add a propTypes object to UserProfile with PropTypes definitions for name, age, and isActive.
steps.expectedOutcome: The UserProfile component will have both TypeScript interface and PropTypes validation.
successCriteria: PropTypes is imported and UserProfile has a propTypes object with PropTypes definitions for name, age, and isActive.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've imported PropTypes and added the propTypes object with all three props defined.
steps.feedbackWrong: The PropTypes weren't properly added. Remember to import PropTypes and add a propTypes object to UserComponent with PropTypes definitions for name, age, and isActive.

steps.title: Create a parent component to pass props
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named App that renders both UserProfile and ProductCard components with appropriate props.
steps.hint: Define a new component that returns JSX containing both components with their required props passed as attributes.
steps.expectedOutcome: A parent App component is created that renders both UserProfile and ProductCard with props passed to demonstrate prop passing between components.
successCriteria: The App component is defined and returns JSX containing both UserProfile and ProductCard components with appropriate props passed.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created the App component, but it doesn't render both UserProfile and ProductCard with appropriate props. Make sure to include both components in the JSX and pass the required props.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component is not properly defined or doesn't render the child components. Create a functional component named App that returns JSX containing both UserProfile and ProductCard with props.

steps.title: Review and test the complete implementation
steps.instruction: Add a final review section to the App component that renders both UserProfile and ProductCard components with sample props to verify TypeScript interfaces and PropTypes work together.
steps.hint: Inside the App component's return statement, add both components with appropriate props that match their interfaces.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component renders both UserProfile and ProductCard components with appropriate props to demonstrate TypeScript interface validation.
successCriteria: UserProfile component receives name, age, and isActive props. ProductCard component receives at least one prop. Both components render within the App component.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure both UserProfile and ProductCard components are rendered with appropriate props that match their interfaces.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component doesn't render both components with appropriate props. Review the component interfaces and ensure you're passing the correct prop values.
